newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-WILLIAMS, GRISSOM LEAD TRIBE PAST YANKS IN SLUGFEST.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-WILLIAMS, GRISSOM LEAD TRIBE PAST YANKS IN SLUGFEST.

text.p: Matt Williams and Marquis Grissom combined for nine hits and nine RBI as the Cleveland Indians won a 12-8 slugfest with the New York Yankees Saturday.
Williams went 4-for-5 with two homers and six RBI and Marquis Grissom was 5-for-6 and drove in three runs to pace Cleveland's 19-hit assault on New York pitching.
Williams hit a two-run homer in a four-run second as Cleveland assumed a 4-3 lead.

New York responded with a run in the second and added two in the third and one in the fourth for a 7-5 advantage. But Cleveland took the lead for good with a six-run sixth, highlighted by Williams's three-run shot off Jim Mecir that made it 11-7.
"It was good to see Matt hit the ball," said Indians manager Mike Hargrove of his slugger who had just five RBI in his previous 29 games.
Tino Martinez belted his 27th homer for the Yanks, a three-run shot off Indians starter Brian Anderson in the first. Cecil Fielder added a two-run homer in the third for New York.

Yankees starter David Wells was rocked for five runs in three innings and Kenny Rogers (4-4), making his second straight appearance out of the bullpen, was roughed up for five runs in 2 1/3 innings to suffer the loss.
Eric Plunk (2-2) picked up the win after allowing a run over two innings in relief of Anderson, who was tagged for six runs in just three innings.
"We wore each other out, we just happened to get them last," said Hargrove.
Cleveland's Sandy Alomar had three hits and drove in a run to extend his hitting streak to 25 games.
In Boston, Felipe Lira allowed two runs over six solid innings and Tony Clark and Melvin Nieves hit solo homers to lead the Detroit Tigers to a 9-2 rout of the Red Sox.
Phil Nevin added a three-run homer in the ninth and had a career-high four RBI for Detroit, which has won three in a row from Boston to escape the American League East cellar.
Lira (5-4) gave up six hits, walked one and struck out three for the win. Aaron Sele (9-6) saw his three-game win streak snapped, allowing four runs and seven hits in 6 1/3 innings.
In Baltimore, Alex Gonzalez, Orlando Merced and Carlos Garcia hit solo homers and three relievers combined for four shutout innings as the Toronto Blue Jays beat the Orioles 5-2.

Woody Williams (3-7) gave up two runs and five hits in five innings before turning the ball over to the Toronto bullpen. Paul Quantrill, Paul Spoljaric and Mike Timlin each worked 1 1/3 innings with Timlin retiring all four batters he faced for his eighth save.
Gonzalez and Merced homered off starter Jimmy Key (11-4) in the top of the third as Baltimore lost its third in a row.

In Kansas City, Jeff D'Amico allowed two earned runs over seven innings for his fourth staight win and Jack Voigt's RBI double capped a three-run sixth as the Milwaukee Brewers snapped a four-game skid with a 5-3 victory over the Royals.
D'Amico (6-3) gave up nine hits and a walk with three strikeouts. He has allowed seven earned runs and 23 hits during his winning streak, spanning 30 2/3 innings.
The Brewers snapped a 2-2 tie with three in the sixth on Jeff Cirillo's RBI single, a sacrifice fly by Dave Nilsson and Voight's double, which plated Cirillo.

At Minnesota, Scott Stahoviak had two hits and two RBI in a seven-run second inning that lasted 33 minutes and Chuck Knoblauch went 4-for-5 with two RBI as the Twins snapped a Chicago White Sox seven-game win streak with an 11-5 romp.
The Twins sent 12 men to the plate and collected eight hits in the second inning, chasing starter Doug Drabek (6-5), who surrendered six runs and seven hits while retiring only four batters.
Knoblauch started the rout in the first with his 11th career leadoff homer.
Brad Radke (9-5) benefited from the Twins' offensive explosion, winning his fifth straight start.
In Oakland, Juan Gonzalez had his third multi-homer game of the year and Darren Oliver combined with three relievers on a five-hitter as the Texas Rangers blanked the Athletics 2-0.
Gonzalez homered on 1-1 counts off Oakland starter Brad Rigby (0-1) in the second and fourth innings for his 15th and 16th round-trippers of the year.
Oliver (4-9) allowed all five hits while walking five and recording seven strikeouts. Danny Patterson tossed 2 2/3 perfect innings and Eric Gunderson and John Wetteland recorded the last four outs.

In Seattle, Allen Watson and Troy Percival combined to hold the American League's most potent offence to three hits and Luis Alicea homered and drove in two runs as the Anaheim Angels topped the Mariners 6-1.
Watson (7-4), who retired 18 straight batters before Jay Buhner singled with two out in the seventh, won for the sixth time in his last seven starts.
Anaheim's Tony Phillips stole home in a four-run seventh that put the Angels up 6-0.
Seattle scored its lone run on a sacrifice fly by Edgar Martinez in the ninth after a Percival wild pitch.
